formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: The signature lets anyone call permit, which sets the USDC allowance of the owner (the signer) for the spender to exactly `value`. It replaces any earlier allowance and does not add to it.
The signature can be used until `deadline`. type(uint256).max means it never expires.
Using the signature increments the signer's permit nonce. No tokens move when it is used: the spender can later pull up to `value` USDC with transferFrom.
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender address, the maximum amount in USDC (or "Unlimited" from 2^255 up), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit test covers only a finite amount; the "Unlimited" threshold and no-expiry deadline paths are untested.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json uses value "250000000" and deadline "1798761600" only. The descriptor field `value` has threshold 0x8000… with message "Unlimited". EIP2612._permit accepts `deadline == type(uint256).max` as no expiration.
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = 2^256-1 (expect "Unlimited") and one with deadline = 2^256-1.

findings.title: Permit deadline type(uint256).max means no expiry, but the date field shows it as a far-future date.
findings.evidence: EIP2612.sol _permit: `require(deadline == type(uint256).max || deadline >= now, ...)`. Descriptor field `deadline` 'Valid until' has format date, encoding timestamp, and no special-value message.
findings.fix: The date format has no threshold or message parameter, so no descriptor change can fix this. A spec extension would allow "No expiry".
